newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast crisis deepens as Jordan rebukes Israel.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crisis deepens as Jordan rebukes Israel.

text.p: An Arab-Israeli crisis deepened on Tuesday with reports Jordan's King Hussein had told Benjamin Netanyahu he didn't trust him and had warned Israel's leader of an impending blow-up of Middle East peace efforts.

Underscoring tensions, an Israeli soldier guarding a West Bank Jewish settlement near Hebron was stabbed 20 times and wounded seriously in an apparent Palestinian guerrilla attack, military sources said. The two attackers fled with his gun.

Israeli officials, who failed to salvage peace moves with the Palestinians in crisis talks on Monday night, confirmed reports by Israeli newspapers that Netanyahu had received a letter from the king but did not divulge its contents.

The Jordanian monarch, who signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, was quoted by Israel's Maariv newspaper as writing to Netanyahu: "You are destroying the peace and I haven't an ounce of trust in you."

The rival daily Yedioth Ahronoth reported the king warned of an "explosion of the peace process" unless Netanyahu reversed his decision to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem captured from Jordan in a 1967 war.

Netanyahu, on an official visit to Moscow, told reporters travelling with him: "There is no place for this cricitism and certainly there is no place for this tone." Officials said he had sent the king a response.

"I expect our partners and our friends in the peace process not to automatically adopt the Palestinian position. We stand on our right to build in Jerusalem, our united capital," Netanyahu said in the remarks broadcast by Israeli army radio.
Palestinians view East Jerusalem, annexed by Israel in 1967, as the capital of their future state and see Israeli building there as prejudicing future negotiations on the city's status.
They were also enraged by a decision of Netanyahu's cabinet to hand over only a third of the West Bank land they had expected in an Israeli troop redeployment due last week.

"There is a crisis and the crisis is becoming worse and worse," a visibly angry Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo said after meeting Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai at a Tel Aviv hotel late on Monday.
Mordechai was in Jordan to meet King Hussein on Tuesday.

In Washington, President Bill Clinton, speaking at a joint news conference with visiting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, said he regretted the Israeli decision to build 6,500 houses in East Jerusalem.
But the president warned Palestinians it would be a "terrible mistake" to resort to violence over the matter.

Abed Rabbo warned on Monday of a possible repetition of violence that erupted in September when Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem. The clashes killed 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.
Israel contends a U.S. note attached to a January peace deal with the PLO leaves the scope of three pullbacks -- due to be completed by mid-1998 -- to Israel's sole discretion.
Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat spurned an Israeli decision on Friday to hand over another nine percent of the West Bank to his self-rule authority. Palestinians expected 30 percent.

Leading Palestinian official Faisal al-Husseini, asked by Israel Radio why Arafat had spurned Netanyahu's phone calls, said on Tuesday: "If Arafat and Netanyahu meet and Netanyahu gives Arafat new orders -- that's not mutual.
"That's hutzpa," he said, using the Hebrew word for "nerve".
